scenario: [LCST.4.5.7]: every string that is not a signed INT_LIT in the 64-bit range parses to null. The rule logs each string whose `::Int?` is null. Covered: a decimal point and an exponent (no float notation on Int); leading and trailing whitespace; a unit suffix with and without `_`; separators a source literal refuses (after a base prefix, leading, trailing, [LLEX.11.1]); an uppercase `0X` prefix; an out-of-range magnitude; an invalid hex digit; and the empty string. PATH PINNED: FN_STRING_TO_INT's runtime adapter. libds's strtoll today skips leading whitespace, so it parses ` 31` and fails this vector; that is the libc-defined behaviour this clause removes.
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    txt: String mutable

rule absent:
    S s where (s.txt::Int?) is null
->
    log info "[{s.txt}]"
